comment: gpt-oss-20B served from the OFFICIAL openai/gpt-oss-20b checkpoint (native
MXFP4 MoE experts). Calibration (rotations + VQ codebook) was captured by
loading this SAME checkpoint and letting transformers dequantize it to
bf16 for the forward passes (Mxfp4Config(dequantize=True) -- there is no
native MXFP4 compute path for calibration) -- see
pipelines/oscar_e2e/gptoss_calibrate.py:108-124 and
logs/build_gptoss_mxfp4*.log ('MXFP4 checkpoint -> dequantizing to bf16').
This is the checkpoint-consistent pairing: compare against
gptoss20b_bf16_v1.json, which calibrates AND serves the unsloth bf16
upcast instead. The two must never be cross-wired (mxfp4 rotations/
codebook served against the unsloth checkpoint or vice versa) -- that
mismatch is exactly what every prior gpt-oss-mxfp4 cell in this repo did
(healthy/vq2mx_* served unsloth/gpt-oss-20b-BF16; niah8k_postmerge served
the real checkpoint but with the OLDER unsloth-calibrated bundle, since
it predates this calibration build by ~2h). No cell has combined the two
correctly yet -- this protocol is what closes that gap.
vq2 = VQ for K (SGLANG_VQ_CODEBOOK_PATH, group-VQ gather kernel) + OSCAR
SST rotation + int2 for V (SGLANG_OSCAR_V_ROTATION_PATH) -- this is what
--vq2 always does in serve_oscar.sh, not a per-protocol choice; K's own
OSCAR rotation/clip env is set but ignored by the VQ encoder.
Three knobs below (moe_runner_backend, quant_group_size=0,
absorb_v_rotation=0) are architecture-mandatory for gpt-oss's hybrid-SWA
layout (12 of 24 layers full-attention; only those get a quant pool), not
protocol choices -- see serve_oscar.sh:160-164 and
notes/page_quant/studies/throughput_benchmark.md 'gpt-oss-20B integration'
for the three boot blockers these work around (MoE routing NameError,
fa3 hybrid-attn crash, absorb-rotation contiguous-layer assumption).
TP=2 and every other serve knob below (max_reqs, kv_splits, cuda_graph_bs,
mem_frac) match the validated recipe in logs/_scratch/boot_vq2_mx.sh and
the report14 SS10.5 shadow-fix study -- not re-derived here.
Task grid is NIAH-only. gpqa_diamond.csv (raw GPQA, unformatted) and
math500_gptoss_32k*.jsonl (question/solution pairs, no prompt/rid/
max_new_tokens) are NOT client-ready rows -- run_prompts_client.py needs
a pre-templated 'prompt' field per record, which only the niah_*_gptoss
exports have. niah_131072 exists but is EXCLUDED: no cell has ever served
gpt-oss above ctx=98304 (the throughput study's validated ceiling, itself
only for bf16); serving 131072 needs ctx >131072, unvalidated on this
stack. Extend ctx and add the task once that's been smoke-tested.
Sampling is greedy/single-sample (T=0.0, samples=1) for every NIAH task --
this matches every validated gpt-oss NIAH cell in the repo (niah8k_*,
healthy/*), NOT the Qwen protocol's T=0.6/3-seed convention. If you want
apples-to-apples sampling with the Qwen grid, that's a deliberate change
from precedent, not a bug -- make it explicitly.
exact_chunked_prefill: false reproduces the published serving default.
This is the SAME open decision as the Qwen protocol, but far more
consequential here -- report14 SS10.4/10.5 measured healthy300 chunk-4096
collapsing 89.00->67.33 (-21.7) without the shadow fix, driven ~3/4 by
VQ-K and ~1/4 by INT2-V. Do not quote a chunked gpt-oss vq2 headline
number without deciding this field first.
Sync note: this protocol's rotations/codebook are manifest group
'gptoss_mxfp4', but the NIAH row files live under manifest group
'gptoss' (shared with gptoss20b_bf16_v1.json). Sync BOTH groups.
